title: Photos on the request
fit: The website says to send a few photos. The request form has nowhere to attach them.

title: Public booking matches the five services
fit: The request form is the front door. Its categories have to match the website.

title: Website and card info edited in the app
fit: The website and your card are how people reach you. They show the same phone and email as your estimates.

title: Sponsored work for any realtor, one form
fit: An agent request should land in the same inbox as a homeowner request.

title: Realtor-sponsored property work
fit: Who pays, and for which house, starts when the request comes in.

title: Seasonal checkup
fit: A blog checkup would open a request already set to Maintenance for that house.

title: Property opportunities
fit: Things the house might need later. Deferred until the property record is boringly reliable.

title: Property health records
fit: A health reading of the house. Deferred with the rest of property intelligence.

title: Maintenance plan fit
fit: Membership expansion is out of scope. The idea stays on the house until that changes.

title: Seller keeps or drops lines
fit: A listing quote needs a yes or no on each line. No backlog task owns that yet.

title: Pay from closing
fit: For the listings you choose, the quote can say payment comes from closing proceeds.

title: Materials estimate trust and calibration
fit: The price on the quote should be one the job can stand behind.

title: Door hardware materials onto the buy list
fit: A known door scope should price itself onto the quote's material list.

title: Room-based estimate templates
fit: Repeatable room scopes belong on the quote, before a job exists.

title: Estimate versioning
fit: A changed price should keep the earlier quote, not overwrite it.

title: Chosen option flows into totals and invoices
fit: When you offer Good/Better/Best, the job and bill should follow the option the customer picked.

title: Change orders reach the bill, prior invoices credited
fit: Extra work needs a customer yes on the quote side, then the bill has to include it.

title: Reconcile estimate calibration
fit: Deferred with the cancelled estimating scaffold. The quote is still where it would land.

title: Work item library
fit: A library of common work would feed quotes. Production intelligence is deferred.

title: Each kind of work estimated its own way
fit: Walls, ceilings, trim and patching on a prepared quote each get their own method, and the quote says what it is missing.

title: Hourly baseline on every quote
fit: Every quote is checked against your hourly rate, whichever screen built it. Your price stays yours.

title: Baseline formula written down first
fit: You approve the math on paper before any code, so nothing is counted twice.

title: Production rates you can edit and calibrate
fit: Your pace numbers live in Settings. Until checked against real jobs, they are labeled uncalibrated.

title: Baseline panel and send checks
fit: See the quote against your hourly rate, and cannot send with hours or costs missing.

title: Review that reads the real quote
fit: The review sees your lines, hours and rates instead of asking for square footage, and runs only when you ask.

title: Painting edit uses your rates
fit: The painting calculator's lines and total use the same rates.

title: Good/Better/Best totals and line types
fit: Option quotes list at a real total and keep their materials lines as materials.

title: Room-by-room pricing saves all or nothing
fit: A failed calculation never leaves a quote with the wrong total.

title: Prepared quote edge cases
fit: A fixed price never vanishes, and the profit card matches the quote lines.

title: Portal approval lands like the email path
fit: When a customer approves on the portal you get told, and a double click does not show them an error.

title: Safer AI calls on quotes
fit: AI answers are checked before use, costly ones are owner-only, and each call's cost is recorded.

title: Materials list never times out
fit: A big materials list finishes instead of showing 'Network error'.

title: Quote cleanup and stale sent quotes
fit: Small quote errors fixed, and old quotes still marked sent get closed out with your OK.

title: Estimating assistant (Phase 3 slice)
fit: Prices on quotes say where they came from and how much to trust them; paint quantities come from your measurements.

title: Price history you can trust
fit: Every price you paid is kept with its source and date, not overwritten.

title: Purchase imports without double counting
fit: Import two years of Home Depot history without booking expenses or counting a purchase twice.

title: Package sizes
fit: The app knows a 1-gallon can from a 5-gallon bucket, and asks when it doesn't.

title: Price confidence with reasons
fit: Each material price says High, Medium, Low or Unverified, and why.

title: Paint pilot
fit: Paint and primer quantities and prices from your rooms and your purchases.

title: Estimated vs actual hours
fit: See how a job's work hours compared with the quote, like for like.

title: More material formulas
fit: Drywall, caulk, trim and supplies, after the paint pilot proves out.

title: Craftsman hours beside your price book
fit: See Craftsman's hours and what each job includes next to your own, as a check. It never changes a price.

title: Check your work rates against Craftsman
fit: The rates that turn square feet and fixtures into hours get a once-over against Craftsman; you decide each one.

title: Save quick materials onto the job
fit: Materials gathered outside a quote still have to land on the job.

title: Change orders checked against your hourly rate
fit: Added work on a job should get the same hours check as the original quote.

title: Text when the day moves
fit: The website says a schedule change comes from you. A moved visit does not text the customer. No task owns it yet.

title: Mileage claim versus GPS
fit: Miles are part of the day at the house, checked when the day is done.

title: Tag miles from Complete
fit: Completing the visit is when untagged miles should get a house.

title: Untagged claim miles leftover
fit: Miles that never got a house stay on the day until someone tags them.

title: Night stop interview
fit: Stops the day did not explain get a question at the end of the day.

title: Hold the stop until the truck leaves
fit: The visit should not split into a new stop while the truck is still there.

title: Field prompts on the phone
fit: Start day, arrival, and the next visit prompt belong on the day of work.

title: Job closeout when the visit is finished
fit: Finishing the visit is the moment the job asks done, or coming back.

title: Done, or coming back
fit: The fork at the end of a visit: finished, or another day.

title: Coming back writes the next visit
fit: If the work continues, the next visit is born from this one.

title: Brief the next person
fit: What this visit learned has to be on the next visit.

title: Night leftovers after closeout
fit: What closeout did not finish shows up that night, still tied to the visit.

title: One next action on Today
fit: Today is the visit screen. It should show the next action and little else.

title: Fewer taps from the visit to the bill
fit: The path from the open visit through materials to the bill should be shorter.

title: Site presence
fit: Knowing you are at the house is a fact about the visit.

title: Visit summary
fit: One summary of what the visit produced, on the visit.

title: Auto-start the job on arrival
fit: Optional. Arrival at a scheduled house could start the visit. Not while closeout is unfinished.

title: A paid bill closes the job
fit: Payment lives on the bill. When it is paid, the job can close.

title: Where a receipt goes
fit: A receipt has to land on the right job and the right bill.

title: Job materials become bill lines
fit: Materials bought for the job should show up as lines the customer can read.

title: Bill summary by area, and itemized receipts
fit: The bill should say what area the work was in, and the customer should reach the receipts.

title: Finishing the job drafts the bill
fit: When the work is done, the next record is the bill.

title: Send the bill through Square
fit: Card or bank payment goes out from the bill, and the link stays.

title: Square fees on the payment
fit: The fee belongs on the payment, so the job knows what it kept.

title: Deposit rule kept from the start
fit: A materials deposit chosen before materials are listed still shows up once they are.

title: Vault lines save reliably
fit: Paint, models, and filters from a job have to land on the house record.

title: Home vault categories
fit: The house record is grouped the way the website describes it.

title: Publish a job report
fit: The report is how a finished visit becomes house history the customer can open.

title: Unpublished jobs stay visible
fit: A finished job with no report is missing history. The queue is there so it is not forgotten.

title: Customer page answers what we did and what is next
fit: The customer reads history here. The page should answer the house, not show a pile of dates.

title: One page for the whole house
fit: A seller needs one page: every job, one photo, and the colors worth keeping.

title: Staff preview of the customer page is read-only
fit: Looking at the customer page must not change their record.

title: Customer can request, edit contact, and print bills
fit: Those actions belong on the customer's own page.

title: Realtor page of work they paid for
fit: An agent looks across houses they paid for. It is a view, not a new kind of job.

title: Desk is the leak list
fit: The office home should show money and promises that are leaking, and little else.

title: Promise capture
fit: A promise you make in the office has to land on a request, quote, job, or bill.

title: UX direction on the working screens
fit: The direction applies to every screen. Desk is where you notice it failing.

title: This map
fit: The map is how you see the system. It stays current in the same change as the work.

title: One inbox for things to review
fit: Review leftovers belong on the office home, not on a second queue.

title: Audit hardening
fit: CI, database roles, and how the app loads. Under the floor, not a step of a job.

title: Row-level security on the web tier
fit: Every query has to stay inside the account. That is plumbing.

title: Backups include uploads and the env file
fit: A backup that skips files or secrets is not a backup.

title: Operational intelligence
fit: Profit figures driving automation. It stays under the floor so it is not mistaken for a step of a job.

title: A gatekeeper on pull requests
fit: Out of scope until it is proven in daily use.

title: Confidence engine
fit: A scorer for production intelligence. Deferred.

title: Password changes are recorded
fit: You can tell when a password was changed. Plumbing, not a job step.
